# Data Preprocessing

In this first chapter, we complete preprocessing steps on the breast cancer
dataset. We begin with a Seurat object exported from AtoMx<sup>&#174;</sup> SIP 
before any processing. We perform quality control to remove low quality cells
and then proceed through normalization, dimension reduction, and cell typing.


```{r}
#| label: loading preamble
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
source("./preamble.R")
```

## QC

In this section we run standard QC steps on the breast cancer dataset.

<details>
<summary>Click to show/hide QC steps</summary>


### Per Cell QC

#### Transcripts per cell

Visualize transcripts per cell.

```{r}
#| label: plot_txPerCell
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| eval: false

# Object and color setup

if (!("seu.obj" %in% ls())){
  seu.obj <- readRDS(results_list$raw_seurat_file)
}

# Plotting XY
ggplot(seu.obj@meta.data, 
       aes(x = x_slide_mm, y = y_slide_mm, color = log10(nCount_RNA))) +
  geom_point(size = 0.001) +
  scale_color_viridis(option = "A") +
  theme_classic() +
  coord_fixed() 
ggsave(filename = paste0(qc_dir, "/Plots/XY_txPerCell.png"),
       width = 16, height = 16, units = "in")

# Plot histogram of tx per cell with cutoffs
lower_tx_cutoff = 200 # Adjust by dataset
upper_tx_cutoff = 15000 # Adjust by dataset
ggplot(seu.obj@meta.data, aes(x = log10(nCount_RNA))) +
  geom_histogram() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = log10(lower_tx_cutoff), color = "red") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = log10(upper_tx_cutoff), color = "red") +
  ylab("Cells") +
  theme_classic()
ggsave(filename = paste0(qc_dir, "/Plots/histogram_txPerCell.png"),
       width = 4, height = 4, units = "in")
results_list$lower_tx_cutoff = lower_tx_cutoff
results_list$upper_tx_cutoff = upper_tx_cutoff
saveRDS(results_list, results_list_file)


```

### Per FOV QC

#### FOVQC
Use the CosMx-specific algorithm [FOVQC](https://nanostring-biostats.github.io/CosMx-Analysis-Scratch-Space/posts/fov-qc/index.html) to check for any FOVs that show loss of signal. 

```{r}
#| label: run_fovQC
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| eval: false

# Object and color setup

if (!("seu.obj" %in% ls())){
  seu.obj <- readRDS(results_list$raw_seurat_file)
}

## Run FOV QC
if (!file.exists(paste0(qc_dir, "/Data/fovqc.RDS"))) {
   source("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Nanostring-Biostats/CosMx-Analysis-Scratch-Space/Main/_code/FOV%20QC/FOV%20QC%20utils.R")  
  allbarcodes <- readRDS(url("https://github.com/Nanostring-Biostats/CosMx-Analysis-Scratch-Space/raw/Main/_code/FOV%20QC/barcodes_by_panel.RDS"))
  barcodes <- allbarcodes[["Hs_WTX"]]
  
  smallfovs <- names(which(table(seu.obj@meta.data$fov) < 500))
  tempuse <- !is.element(seu.obj@meta.data$fov, smallfovs)
  
  sharedgenes <- intersect(barcodemap[,1], rownames(seu.obj@assays$RNA@counts))
  res <- runFOVQC(counts = t(seu.obj@assays$RNA@counts)[tempuse, sharedgenes], 
                  xy = seu.obj@meta.data[,c("x_slide_mm", "y_slide_mm")][tempuse, ], 
                  fov = as.character(seu.obj@meta.data$fov[tempuse]), 
                  barcodemap = barcodemap[match(sharedgenes, barcodemap[, 1]), ],
                  max_prop_loss = 0.5, max_totalcounts_loss = 0.5)  
  str(res)
  saveRDS(res, file = paste0(qc_dir, "/Data/fovqc.RDS"))
} else {
  res <- readRDS(paste0(qc_dir, "/Data/fovqc.RDS"))
}

# Plot FOV QC results following FOV QC vignette from Scratch Space.

# Show flagged FOVs in space
png(filename = paste0(qc_dir, "/Plots/flagged_FOVs_in_space.png"), 
    width = 8, height = 6, units = "in", res = 300)
mapFlaggedFOVs(res)
dev.off()

# Plot loss in total signal strength:
png(filename = paste0(qc_dir, "/Plots/overall_signal_loss_in_space.png"), 
    width = 8, height = 6, units = "in", res = 300)
FOVSignalLossSpatialPlot(res, shownames = TRUE)
dev.off()

```
Flagged FOVs in space:
```{r}
knitr::include_graphics(paste0(qc_dir, "/Plots/flagged_FOVs_in_space.png"))
```
There is one FOV that gets flagged due to low counts. As this is on the edge of the tissue, this is not too surprising and we will keep this FOV in our analysis.

Loss in total signal strength:
```{r}
knitr::include_graphics(paste0(qc_dir, "/Plots/overall_signal_loss_in_space.png"))
```
The changes in total signal strength tend to follow biology and do not track with individual FOVs. Thus, we will not exclude any FOVs for further analysis based on these results.

### Cell Flagging

Flag cells that failed any of the QC above and plot these in space. We're looking for areas with high failure rates, suggesting technical artifacts (local tissue peeling, blurriness, etc).

```{r}
#| label: flag_cells
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| eval: false

# Object and color setup

if (!("seu.obj" %in% ls())){
  seu.obj <- readRDS(results_list$raw_seurat_file)
}

# Flag cells that failed tx or area QC
seu.obj@meta.data <- seu.obj@meta.data %>%
  mutate(qcCellsFlagged = case_when(
    Area.um2 > area_cutoff ~ "TRUE",
    nCount_RNA < lower_tx_cutoff ~ "TRUE",
    nCount_RNA > upper_tx_cutoff ~ "TRUE",
    TRUE ~ "FALSE"
  ))

# Plotting XY
ggplot(seu.obj@meta.data, 
       aes(x = x_slide_mm, y = y_slide_mm, color = qcCellsFlagged)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.001) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "lightgrey", "TRUE" = "red")) +
  theme_classic() +
  coord_fixed() 
ggsave(filename = paste0(qc_dir, "/Plots/XY_QCflaggedCells.png"),
       width = 16, height = 16, units = "in")

# Remove cells failing QC and save seurat object
seu.obj <- seu.obj[,which(seu.obj@meta.data$qcCellsFlagged == "FALSE")]
saveRDS(seu.obj, file = paste0(objects_dir, "/seurat_object_postQC.rds"))
results_list$seurat_file_postQC = paste0(objects_dir, "/seurat_object_postQC.rds")
  saveRDS(results_list, results_list_file)


```

Flagged cells in XY space:

```{r}
knitr::include_graphics(paste0(qc_dir, "/Plots/XY_QCflaggedCells.png"))
```

From this plot, it's clear that the flagged cells aren't evenly spread across the tissue - there are round-ish structures that are getting flagged at a much higher rate, suggesting that there's a structure in the tissue that has lower counts for some reason. Given this, we have used a liberal cutoff of 200 counts per cell. From a bit of exploration, it's clear that these cells are primarily getting flagged due to having low counts. Returning to the immunofluorescence images, these likely mark regions of necrosis.

### Total counts normalization
Run total counts normalization with Seurat function.

```{r}
#| label: run_tcNorm
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| eval: false

# Object and color setup

if (!("seu.obj" %in% ls())){
```

## Cell Typing

In this section we assign major and minor cell types using a combination of
iterative unsupervised clustering and marker-based hierarchical assignment.

<details>
<summary>Click to show/hide cell typing steps</summary>

This section performs cell typing of the dataset with a multistep approach. 
First, we use unsupervised clustering to broadly group the cells. For some of 
these major cell types (tumor cells, fibroblasts, vascular cells) we subset and 
perform unsupervised clustering a second time on the subset. For immune cells, 
we use the marker-based hierarchical cell typing approach HieraType. 

### Unsupervised clustering
Cluster cells with Seurat function.

```{r}
#| label: run_leidenCluster
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| eval: false

if (!("seu.obj" %in% ls())){
  seu.obj <- readRDS(results_list$seurat_file_postUMAP)
}

# With Seurat
seu.obj <- Seurat::FindClusters(seu.obj, graph.name = "umapgrph", resolution = 0.7)

# Plot it in XY space with random colors
set.seed(2024)
my_pal <- sample(colors(distinct = TRUE), length(unique(seu.obj@meta.data$seurat_clusters)))
names(my_pal) <- as.character(unique(seu.obj@meta.data$seurat_clusters))
ggplot(seu.obj@meta.data,
        aes(x = x_slide_mm, y = y_slide_mm, 
            color = as.factor(seurat_clusters))) +  
    geom_point(size = 0.1) +  
  scale_color_manual(values = my_pal) +
    theme_classic() +  
    coord_fixed() +  
    guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size=10)))
ggsave(filename = paste0(dimRed_dir, "/Plots/XY_leiden.png"),
       width = 8, height = 16, units = "in")

# Plot each cell type separately
for (ct in unique(seu.obj@meta.data$seurat_clusters)){
  ggplot(seu.obj@meta.data[order(seu.obj@meta.data$seurat_clusters == ct),],
         aes(x = x_slide_mm, y = y_slide_mm, 
             color = seurat_clusters==ct)) +  
    geom_point(size = 0.05) +  
    scale_color_manual(values = c("lightgrey", "red"), name = ct) +
    theme_classic() +  
    coord_fixed() +  
    guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size=10)))
  ggsave(filename = paste0(dimRed_dir, "/Plots/XY_leiden_", ct, ".png"),
         width = 8, height = 16, units = "in")
}


# Plot it in UMAP space
DimPlot(seu.obj, group.by = "seurat_clusters", reduction = "umap", label = T) +
  scale_color_manual(values = my_pal)
ggsave(filename = paste0(dimRed_dir, "/Plots/umap_leiden.png"))

# Plot each cell type separately in UMAP space
plot.df <- seu.obj@meta.data
plot.df$UMAP1 <- seu.obj@reductions$umap@cell.embeddings[,1]
plot.df$UMAP2 <- seu.obj@reductions$umap@cell.embeddings[,2]

for (ct in unique(plot.df$seurat_clusters)){
  ggplot(plot.df[order(plot.df$seurat_clusters == ct),],
         aes(x = UMAP1, y = UMAP2, 
             color = seurat_clusters==ct)) +  
    geom_point(size = 0.05, alpha = 0.5) +  
    scale_color_manual(values = c("lightgrey", "red"), name = ct) +
    theme_classic() +  
    coord_fixed() +  
    guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size=10)))
  ggsave(filename = paste0(dimRed_dir, "/Plots/UMAP_leiden_", ct, ".png"),
         width = 10, height = 8, units = "in")
}

# Generate a marker heatmap with HieraType functions
## prepare data for marker gene heatmap:
fc_subclus_ctl_gran <- clusterwise_foldchange_metrics(seu.obj[["RNA"]]@counts
                                                      ,metadata = seu.obj@meta.data
                                                      ,cluster_column = "seurat_clusters"
)
# subtract background from the mean per-cluster expression profiles:
neg_counts <- seu.obj@assays$negprobes$counts
for (name in unique(seu.obj@meta.data$seurat_clusters)) {
  isthiscelltype <- seu.obj@meta.data$seurat_clusters == name
  meannegthiscelltype <- Matrix::mean(neg_counts[, isthiscelltype])
  
  fc_subclus_ctl_gran$cluster_expr[fc_subclus_ctl_gran$cluster == name] <- 
    pmax(fc_subclus_ctl_gran$cluster_expr[fc_subclus_ctl_gran$cluster == name] - meannegthiscelltype, 0)
}
# create the heatmap:
hm_semiSup <- add_ncells(marker_heatmap(fc_subclus_ctl_gran))

png(filename = paste0(dimRed_dir, "/Plots/heatmap_leiden_negRemoved.png"),
    width = 24, height = 8, units = "in", res = 300)
print(hm_semiSup)
dev.off()

# Save seurat object
results_list$leiden_color_pal <- my_pal
results_list$seurat_file_postLeiden <- paste0(objects_dir, "/seurat_object_postLeiden.rds")
saveRDS(results_list, results_list_file)
saveRDS(seu.obj, results_list$seurat_file_postLeiden)

```

```{r}
knitr::include_graphics(paste0(dimRed_dir, "/Plots/XY_leiden.png"))
```

### Refine cell type annotations

These unsupervised clusters do a pretty good job of splitting apart major cell types. We follow this up by naming and refining this initial clustering result based on spatial distribution, top marker genes, and position in UMAP space. In particular, we'll recluster the tumor cells on their own to reduce the number of clusters and subcluster the fibroblast and vascular clusters. Additionally, we'll use HieraType to perform targeted marker-based annotation of the immune cells. We start with our evaluation and planned actions for each cluster:

| Cell type | Evaluation | Refinement |
|-----------|------------|-------------|
| 0         |Tumor, lower lobe        |Tumor recluster       |
| 1         |Tumor, lower lobe        |Tumor recluster       |
| 2         |Fibroblasts, markers LUM, THBS1, AEBP1          |Fibroblast subcluster             |
| 3         |Immune, myeloid         |Immune HieraType             |
| 4         |Tumor, between lobes      |Tumor recluster             |
| 5         |Tumor, exterior of upper lobe       |Tumor recluster             |
| 6         |Immune      |Immune HieraType            |
| 7         |Tumor, exterior of lower lobe      |Tumor recluster         |
| 8         |Tumor, spotty      |Tumor recluster       |
| 9         |Vasculature    |Vasculature subcluster        |
| 10        | Tumor, lower lobe   |Tumor recluster    |
| 11         |Low count cells near tissue gaps. Necrotic cells.     |Rename necrotic cells         |
| 12         |Tumor, upper lobe         |Tumor recluster         |
| 13         |Tumor, interior of upper lobe         |Tumor recluster             |
| 14         |Tumor, adjacent to necrotic zones     |Tumor recluster         |
| 15         |Plasma cells two clusters in UMAP space          |Immune HieraType     |
| 16         |Immune, proliferative        |Immune HieraType             |
| 17         |Small number of border cells and well defined small clusters, potentially healthy epithelia        |Rename Unknown             |

:::{.panel-tabset}

#### Fibroblast subcluster

We start with fibroblasts since this cluster is near immune clusters and may be partially overlapping. The initial unsupervised clustering had only one fibroblast cluster, but from previous experience with this sample we expect that we should be able to identify a few subtypes. Additionally, it appears that the cluster that is mostly fibroblast may also contain some immune cells. Here we take the fibroblast cells, repeat initial preprocessing so that highly variable genes are chosen based on these cells, and use unsupervised clustering to separate these cells into multiple clusters, some of which we'll add to the immune cells for HieraType clustering.
```{r}
#| label: run_leiden_fibroblast_cluster
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| eval: false

if (!("seu.obj" %in% ls())){
  seu.obj <- readRDS(results_list$seurat_file_postLeiden)
}

# Subset the seurat object to only include fibroblast cluster
fibro_leiden <- c(2)
fibro_idx <- which(seu.obj@meta.data$seurat_clusters %in% fibro_leiden)
seu.fibro <- seu.obj[,fibro_idx]

# Repeat preprocessing, dimension reduction, and leiden clustering
seu.fibro <- NormalizeData(seu.fibro, 
                         normalization.method = "RC", 
                         scale.factor = mean(seu.fibro@meta.data$nCount_RNA))
seu.fibro <- FindVariableFeatures(seu.fibro, 
                                selection.method = "vst", 
                                nfeatures = 3000)
seu.fibro <- ScaleData(seu.fibro)
seu.fibro <- RunPCA(seu.fibro, 
                  features = VariableFeatures(seu.fibro))
umapobj <- make_umap(seu.fibro@reductions$pca@cell.embeddings)

seu.fibro[["umap"]] <- umapobj$ump
seu.fibro[["umapgrph"]] <- Seurat::as.Graph(umapobj$grph)
seu.fibro <- Seurat::FindClusters(seu.fibro, graph.name = "umapgrph", resolution = 0.8)

# Save this Seurat object and assignments to files
saveRDS(seu.fibro, file = paste0(objects_dir, "/seurat_fibro_obj.rds"))
fibro_assignments <- seu.fibro@meta.data[,c("cell_ID", "seurat_clusters")]
saveRDS(fibro_assignments, file = paste0(celltyping_dir, "/Data/fibro_cluster_assignments.rds"))

# Save a few quick plots for evaluation
DimPlot(seu.fibro) + coord_fixed()
ggsave(file = paste0(celltyping_dir, "/Plots/UMAP_fibroblast.png"))

# Marker heatmap
## prepare data for marker gene heatmap:
fc_subclus_ctl_gran <- clusterwise_foldchange_metrics(seu.fibro[["RNA"]]@counts
                                                      ,metadata = seu.fibro@meta.data
                                                      ,cluster_column = "seurat_clusters"
)
# subtract background from the mean per-cluster expression profiles:
neg_counts_fibro = seu.fibro@assays$negprobes$counts
for (name in unique(seu.fibro@meta.data$seurat_clusters)) {
  if(is.na(name)){next}
  isthiscelltype <- seu.fibro@meta.data$seurat_clusters == name
  meannegthiscelltype <- Matrix::mean(neg_counts_fibro[, isthiscelltype])
  
  fc_subclus_ctl_gran$cluster_expr[fc_subclus_ctl_gran$cluster == name] <- 
    pmax(fc_subclus_ctl_gran$cluster_expr[fc_subclus_ctl_gran$cluster == name] - meannegthiscelltype, 0)
}
# create the heatmap:
hm_lh <- add_ncells(marker_heatmap(fc_subclus_ctl_gran))

png(filename = paste0(dimRed_dir, "/Plots/heatmap_fibroblast_subcluster_negRemoved.png"),
    width = 24, height = 8, units = "in", res = 300)
print(hm_lh)
dev.off()



```

Based on the markers present, we can see that there are multiple non-fibroblast cell subtypes contained within this cluster. We name the fibroblast subtypes and note the immune subtypes to put into the immune-focused hieratype subtyping.

| Cell type | Evaluation | Name |
|-----------|------------|-------------|
| 0         |Key markers CCN1, CCN2        |Myofibroblasts       |
| 1         |Key markers COL6A6, MMP11       |Matrix fibroblasts       |
| 2         |APC markers HLA-DRA, C1QC          |Immune subtype             |
| 3         |T cell markers TRBC1, IL2RB        |Immune subtype   |
| 4         |Key markers FOS, PTGIS, EGR1   |iCAFs    |
| 5         |Inflammatory markers S100A8/A9   |Immune subtype   |
| 6       |Metabolic markers MUCL1, PIP, FABP7, unclear where to put these. Choosing based on XY and UMAP localization.   |Immune subtype   |
| 7         |Proliferation markers histones. Choosing based on UMAP proximity.    |Immune subtype   |
| 8           |B cell markers MS4A1, BANK1   |Immune subtype   |
| 9           |Key markers CXCL10, IDO1   |Interferon-activated CAFs    |
| 10        |Plasma markers IGHA1, IGKC, JCHAIN   |Immune subtype   |
| 11        |Markers CST1/2, MMP7, unclear. Choosing based on UMAP localization.    |Immune subtype   |
| 12        |Immune markers MMP9, SPP1    |Immune subtype     |

Add cell type names to fibroblast subtypes.
```{r}
#| label: add_fibro_subtype_names
#| message: false

# Follows table above. Any that are not fibroblasts will be listed as NA
fibro_assignments <- readRDS(file = paste0(celltyping_dir, "/Data/fibro_cluster_assignments.rds"))
fibro_assignments$minor_cell_type <- NA
fibro_assignments$minor_cell_type[which(fibro_assignments$seurat_clusters == 0)] <- "Myofibroblasts"
fibro_assignments$minor_cell_type[which(fibro_assignments$seurat_clusters == 1)] <- "Matrix fibroblasts"
fibro_assignments$minor_cell_type[which(fibro_assignments$seurat_clusters == 4)] <- "Inflammatory CAFs"
fibro_assignments$minor_cell_type[which(fibro_assignments$seurat_clusters == 9)] <- "Interferon-activated CAFs"
saveRDS(fibro_assignments, file = paste0(celltyping_dir, "/Data/fibro_cluster_assignments.rds"))

```

#### Immune HieraType

To better assign the immune cells, we use [HieraType](https://nanostring-biostats.github.io/CosMx-Analysis-Scratch-Space/posts/immune-cell-typing-smooth/), a marker-based approach to assigning cell types. We start with marker-based gene lists included in the HieraType package and add in some additional cell subtypes that we expect to be present in this dataset. As described in the table above, we'll use unsupervised clusters 3, 6, 15, and 16 for this immune classification as well as some of the fibroblast subclusters.

```{r}
#| label: run_hieratype_leiden_immune
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| eval: false

if (!("seu.obj" %in% ls())){
  seu.obj <- readRDS(results_list$seurat_file_postLeiden)
}

### Pipeline, with 
### level-1 ('l1') being classification of major immune cell categories
### level-t ('lt') being T8/T4 classification
### level-t4 ('lt4') being further T4 subclassification
### level-t8 ('lt8') being further T8 subclassification
### level-m3 ('m3') being TAM subclassification
### level-p2 ('p2') being plasma subclassification

# All of the above are in HieraType package except plasma and macrophage subclassification
# Here are the plasma subtyping marker lists we'll use:

  HieraType::make_markerslist(
    index_marker = list(
      "Plasma_IgA" = c("IGHA1", "IGHA2", "JCHAIN"),
      "Plasma_IgG" = c("IGHG1", "IGHG2", "IGHG3", "IGHG4")

                       "DERL3", "HSPA5", "CALR", "PDIA4", "PDIA6", "PPIB", "CANX", "SYVN1", "FKBP11",
                       "SDC1","CD38","PRDM1","XBP1","IRF4","SLAMF7",

                       "ITGA4","ITGB7","CCR9","CCR10","ITGAE","MME","CXCR3","CXCR4",
                       "IL10RA","IL10RB","LTB","TGFBR1","PIgR","XBP1","MZB1","DERL3",
                       "SEC61A1","SSR1","SPCS3","FCRL4","POU2AF1","IL6R","IL6ST",
                       "TNFRSF13B","TNFRSF13C","TNFRSF17","AICDA","BACH2","HSPA5","CD10"),
      "Plasma_IgG" = c("CD38", "CD27", "CD138", "TNFRSF17", "IRF4", "XBP1", "PRDM1", "CXCR4", "HLA-DRA",
                       "CD19", "CD79A", "CD79B", "CD40", "CD44", "CD45", "KLF4", "CXCR3", "HSP90B1", "SEC61A1",
                       "DERL3", "HSPA5", "CALR", "PDIA4", "PDIA6", "PPIB", "CANX", "SYVN1", "FKBP11", "MZB1", "JCHAIN",

        "NOS2", "IL12B", "CD80", "CD86", "IRF5", "CXCL9", "CXCL10", "TNF", "IL1B", "NLRP3",

# We add plasma cells and modify the lists for monocytes and neutrophils in the immune marker list
markerslist_immune_modified <- HieraType::markerslist_immune

markerslist_immune_modified$plasma = markerslist_l1$plasma

# Make new marker lists for neutrophil
markerslist_Neu <- 
  HieraType::make_markerslist(
    index_marker = list(
      "neutrophil" = c("MPO", "FCGR3B", "CSF3R")
    ),
    predictors = list(
        "neutrophil" = c("S100A12", "CAMP", "BPI", "LTF", "DEFA3", "RETN", "OLFM4", "MMP8", "FPR1", "FPR2",
                       "CXCR2", "CXCL1", "CXCL8", "IL1R2", "CD177", "S100A11", "HP", "CEACAM6", "RBP7", "ELF3",
                       "SLC22A4", "SLC22A5", "ITGAX", "TNFRSF10C", "PI3", "MME", "RNASE3", "MS4A3", "SIGLEC5", "PRTN3",
                       "AZU1", "ELANE", "CSF3R", "G0S2", "NAAA", "ALOX5", "MMP25", "SERPINB1", "SERPINB10", "CEACAM1",
                       "NFKBIZ", "PLSCR1", "ADGRE3", "LYPD3", "TNFAIP6", "CD24", "PADI4", "TCN1", "LILRA3", "LILRB3",
                       "CRISP3", "NFE2L2", "RNASE2", "RNASE6", "GNB2L1", "ARG1", "ATP6V0D2", "MGST1", "GZMK", "CD63",
                       "CFD", "SERPINA1", "SLC25A37", "SLC11A1", "TLR8", "XBP1", 
                       "DUSP6", "SCN3B", "CALR", "GFI1", "ZBTB16", "S100A8", "S100A9")
    )
  )

# Add back to markers list
markerslist_immune_modified$neutrophil <- markerslist_Neu$neutrophil
markerslist_immune_modified <- markerslist_immune_modified[which(names(markerslist_immune_modified) != "monocyte")]

# Restore markerslist class
class(markerslist_immune_modified) <- unique(c(class(markerslist_immune_modified), "markerslist"))

# Modify the T cell subtypes
markerslist_cd4t_modified <- HieraType::markerslist_cd4tminor
names(markerslist_cd4t_modified) <- dplyr::recode(names(markerslist_cd4t_modified),
                                                  "cd4_th1" = "cd4_teff_th1",
                                                  "cd4_th2" = "cd4_teff_th2",
                                                  "cd4_th17" = "cd4_teff_th17")

markerslist_cd8t_modified <- HieraType::markerslist_cd8tminor
names(markerslist_cd8t_modified) <- dplyr::recode(names(markerslist_cd8t_modified),
                                                  "cd8_cytotoxic" = "cd8_teff_cytotoxic")


pipeline_io_mod <- HieraType::make_pipeline(
  markerslists = list("l1" = markerslist_immune_modified,
                      "lt" = HieraType::markerslist_tcellmajor,
                      "lt4" = markerslist_cd4t_modified,
                      "lt8" = markerslist_cd8t_modified,
                      "m3" = markerslist_m3,
                      "p2" = markerslist_p2
  )
  ,priors = list("lt" = "l1"
                 ,"lt4" = "lt"
                 ,"lt8" = "lt"
                 ,"m3" = "l1"
                 ,"p2" = "l1"
                 ) 
  ,priors_category = list("lt" = "tcell"
                          ,"lt4" = "cd4t"
                          ,"lt8" = "cd8t"
                          ,"m3" = "macrophage"
                          ,"p2" = "plasma"
  )
)

# Save this modified pipeline
saveRDS(pipeline_io_mod, file = paste0(dimRed_dir, "/Data/pipeline_io_mod.rds"))

# Extract immune cells as defined by unsupervised clustering
leiden_immune <- c(3, 6, 15, 16)
idx <- which(seu.obj@meta.data$seurat_clusters %in% leiden_immune)

# Also extract immune cell IDs from cells that had been clustered with fibroblasts
extra_immune <- rownames(fibro_assignments)[which(fibro_assignments$seurat_clusters %in% c(2,3,5:8,10:12))]
idx_immune <- which(seu.obj@meta.data$cell_id %in% extra_immune)

idx <- c(idx,idx_immune)

# Run HieraType to subtype immune cells
immune_typing <- 
run_pipeline(pipeline = pipeline_io_mod
             ,counts_matrix = Matrix::t(seu.obj[["RNA"]]@counts[,idx])
             ,adjacency_matrix = as(seu.obj@graphs$umapgrph[idx,idx]
                                    ,"CsparseMatrix")
             ,celltype_call_threshold = 0.5
             )
saveRDS(immune_typing, file = paste0(dimRed_dir, "/Data/immune_hieratype_res.rds"))

# Add to Seurat object
seu.obj@meta.data$leiden_hieratype <- NA
seu.obj@meta.data[immune_typing$post_probs$l1$cell_ID, "leiden_hieratype"] <-  immune_typing$post_probs$l1$celltype_granular # Use the granular cell type since we're confident these are immune cells.
```

#### Tumor subcluster

The initial unsupervised clustering had more tumor subclusters than we'll use in this analysis. Here we take all the tumor cells, repeat initial preprocessing so that highly variable genes are chosen based on the tumor cells, and use Leiden clustering with low resolution to separate the tumor cells into about five major clusters.
```{r}
#| label: run_leiden_tumor_cluster
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| eval: false

if (!("seu.obj" %in% ls())){
  seu.obj <- readRDS(results_list$seurat_file_postLeiden)
}

# Subset the seurat object to only include tumor cells
tumor_leiden <- c(0, 1, 4, 5, 7, 8, 10, 12:14)
tumor_idx <- which(seu.obj@meta.data$seurat_clusters %in% tumor_leiden)
seu.tumor <- seu.obj[,tumor_idx]

# Repeat preprocessing, dimension reduction, and leiden clustering
seu.tumor <- NormalizeData(seu.tumor, 
                         normalization.method = "RC", 
                         scale.factor = mean(seu.tumor@meta.data$nCount_RNA))
seu.tumor <- FindVariableFeatures(seu.tumor, 
                                selection.method = "vst", 
                                nfeatures = 3000)
seu.tumor <- ScaleData(seu.tumor)
seu.tumor <- RunPCA(seu.tumor, 
                  features = VariableFeatures(seu.tumor))
umapobj <- make_umap(seu.tumor@reductions$pca@cell.embeddings)

seu.tumor[["umap"]] <- umapobj$ump
seu.tumor[["umapgrph"]] <- Seurat::as.Graph(umapobj$grph)
seu.tumor <- Seurat::FindClusters(seu.tumor, graph.name = "umapgrph", resolution = 0.2)

# Save this Seurat object and assignments to files
saveRDS(seu.tumor, file = paste0(objects_dir, "/seurat_tumor_obj.rds"))
tumor_assignments <- seu.tumor@meta.data[,c("cell_ID", "seurat_clusters")]
saveRDS(tumor_assignments, file = paste0(celltyping_dir, "/Data/tumor_cluster_assignments.rds"))
```

```{r}
                                                      ,cluster_column = "seurat_clusters"
)
# subtract background from the mean per-cluster expression profiles:
neg_counts_tumor = seu.tumor@assays$negprobes$counts
for (name in unique(seu.tumor@meta.data$seurat_clusters)) {
  if(is.na(name)){next}
  isthiscelltype <- seu.tumor@meta.data$seurat_clusters == name
  meannegthiscelltype <- Matrix::mean(neg_counts_tumor[, isthiscelltype])
  
  fc_subclus_ctl_gran$cluster_expr[fc_subclus_ctl_gran$cluster == name] <- 
    pmax(fc_subclus_ctl_gran$cluster_expr[fc_subclus_ctl_gran$cluster == name] - meannegthiscelltype, 0)
}
```

#### Vasculature subcluster

The initial Leiden clustering had only one vasculature cluster, but from previous experience with this sample we expect that we should be able to identify pericytes and endothelial cells separately. Here we take the vasculature cells, repeat initial preprocessing so that highly variable genes are chosen based on these cells, and use unsupervised clustering to separate these cells into two or three clusters.
```{r}
#| label: run_leiden_vasculature_cluster
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| eval: false

if (!("seu.obj" %in% ls())){
  seu.obj <- readRDS(results_list$seurat_file_postLeiden)
}

# Subset the seurat object to only include tumor cells
vasc_leiden <- c(9)
vasc_idx <- which(seu.obj@meta.data$seurat_clusters %in% vasc_leiden)
seu.vasc <- seu.obj[,vasc_idx]

# Repeat preprocessing, dimension reduction, and leiden clustering
seu.vasc <- NormalizeData(seu.vasc, 
                         normalization.method = "RC", 
                         scale.factor = mean(seu.vasc@meta.data$nCount_RNA))
seu.vasc <- FindVariableFeatures(seu.vasc, 
                                selection.method = "vst", 
                                nfeatures = 3000)
seu.vasc <- ScaleData(seu.vasc)
seu.vasc <- RunPCA(seu.vasc, 
                  features = VariableFeatures(seu.vasc))
umapobj <- make_umap(seu.vasc@reductions$pca@cell.embeddings)

seu.vasc[["umap"]] <- umapobj$ump
seu.vasc[["umapgrph"]] <- Seurat::as.Graph(umapobj$grph)
seu.vasc <- Seurat::FindClusters(seu.vasc, graph.name = "umapgrph", resolution = 0.1)

# Save this Seurat object and assignments to files
saveRDS(seu.vasc, file = paste0(objects_dir, "/seurat_vasc_obj.rds"))
vasc_assignments <- seu.vasc@meta.data[,c("cell_ID", "seurat_clusters")]
saveRDS(vasc_assignments, file = paste0(celltyping_dir, "/Data/vasc_cluster_assignments.rds"))

# Save a few quick plots for evaluation
# Plot it in XY space with random colors
set.seed(2025)
my_pal <- sample(colors(distinct = TRUE), length(unique(seu.vasc@meta.data$seurat_clusters)))
names(my_pal) <- unique(seu.vasc@meta.data$seurat_clusters)
ggplot(seu.vasc@meta.data,
        aes(x = x_slide_mm, y = y_slide_mm, 
            color = as.factor(seurat_clusters))) +  
    geom_point(size = 0.01) +  
  scale_color_manual(values = my_pal, na.value = "lightgrey") +
    theme_classic() +  
    coord_fixed() +  
    guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size=10)))
ggsave(filename = paste0(celltyping_dir, "/Plots/XY_vasculature_subclusters.png"),
       width = 8, height = 16, units = "in")

# Plot each cell type separately
for (ct in unique(seu.vasc@meta.data$seurat_clusters)){
  if(is.na(ct)){next}
  ggplot(seu.vasc@meta.data,
         aes(x = x_slide_mm, y = y_slide_mm)) +  
    geom_point(size = 0.05, color = "lightgrey") +  
    geom_point(data = seu.vasc@meta.data %>% filter(seurat_clusters == ct),
               aes(x = x_slide_mm, y = y_slide_mm),
               size = 0.05, color = "red") +
    theme_classic() +  
    coord_fixed() +  
    ggtitle(paste0("Vascular subtype: ", ct))
  ggsave(filename = paste0(celltyping_dir, "/Plots/XY_vasculature_subtype_", ct, ".png"),
         width = 8, height = 16, units = "in")
}



# UMAP
DimPlot(seu.vasc) + coord_fixed()
ggsave(file = paste0(celltyping_dir, "/Plots/UMAP_vasculature.png"))

# Marker heatmap
## prepare data for marker gene heatmap:
fc_subclus_ctl_gran <- clusterwise_foldchange_metrics(seu.vasc[["RNA"]]@counts
                                                      ,metadata = seu.vasc@meta.data
                                                      ,cluster_column = "seurat_clusters"
)
# subtract background from the mean per-cluster expression profiles:
neg_counts_vasc = seu.vasc@assays$negprobes$counts
for (name in unique(seu.vasc@meta.data$seurat_clusters)) {
  if(is.na(name)){next}
  isthiscelltype <- seu.vasc@meta.data$seurat_clusters == name
  meannegthiscelltype <- Matrix::mean(neg_counts_vasc[, isthiscelltype])
  
  fc_subclus_ctl_gran$cluster_expr[fc_subclus_ctl_gran$cluster == name] <- 
    pmax(fc_subclus_ctl_gran$cluster_expr[fc_subclus_ctl_gran$cluster == name] - meannegthiscelltype, 0)
}
# create the heatmap:
hm_lh <- add_ncells(marker_heatmap(fc_subclus_ctl_gran))

png(filename = paste0(celltyping_dir, "/Plots/heatmap_vasculature_subcluster_negRemoved.png"),
    width = 12, height = 4, units = "in", res = 300)
print(hm_lh)
dev.off()
```

#### Merging annotations

Here we join all the above annotations into the full Seurat object. We make two cell typing columns - one shows major cell types (tumor, T cell, etc) and the second shows the finer minor cell subtypes. We also make standard plots to show each of these.

```{r}
#| label: merge_plot_cell_subtypes
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| eval: false

if (!("seu.obj" %in% ls())){
  seu.obj <- readRDS(results_list$seurat_file_postLeiden)
}

# Read in cell subtyping results
fibro_assignments <- readRDS(file = paste0(celltyping_dir, "/Data/fibro_cluster_assignments.rds"))
immune_typing <- readRDS(file = paste0(dimRed_dir, "/Data/immune_hieratype_res.rds"))
tumor_assignments <- readRDS(file = paste0(celltyping_dir, "/Data/tumor_cluster_assignments.rds"))
vasc_assignments <- readRDS(file = paste0(celltyping_dir, "/Data/vasc_cluster_assignments.rds"))

# Extract immune typing assignments to same format as other subtypings
immune_assignments <- as.data.frame(immune_typing$post_probs$l1)
row.names(immune_assignments) <- immune_assignments$cell_ID

# Add fine subtypes to seurat object
seu.obj@meta.data$minor_cell_type <- NA
seu.obj@meta.data[fibro_assignments$cell_ID, "minor_cell_type"] <- fibro_assignments$minor_cell_type
seu.obj@meta.data[tumor_assignments$cell_ID, "minor_cell_type"] <- tumor_assignments$minor_cell_type
seu.obj@meta.data[vasc_assignments$cell_ID, "minor_cell_type"] <- vasc_assignments$minor_cell_type
seu.obj@meta.data[immune_assignments$cell_ID, "minor_cell_type"] <- immune_assignments$celltype_granular

# Two clusters that did not get subtyped
seu.obj@meta.data$minor_cell_type[which(seu.obj@meta.data$seurat_clusters == 11)] <- "Necrotic cells"
seu.obj@meta.data$minor_cell_type[which(seu.obj@meta.data$seurat_clusters == 17)] <- "Unknown"

# Add major types
seu.obj@meta.data$major_cell_type <- seu.obj@meta.data$minor_cell_type
seu.obj@meta.data$major_cell_type <- dplyr::recode(seu.obj@meta.data$major_cell_type,
                                                   "cd4_naive" = "Tcell",
                                                   "cd4_tcm" = "Tcell",
                                                   "cd4_teff_th1" = "Tcell",
                                                   "cd4_teff_th2" = "Tcell",
                                                   "cd4_teff_th17" = "Tcell",
                                                   "cd4_tem" = "Tcell",
                                                   "cd4_treg" = "Tcell",
                                                   "cd8_exhausted" = "Tcell",
                                                   "cd8_naive" = "Tcell",
                                                   "cd8_tcm" = "Tcell",
                                                   "cd8_teff_cytotoxic" = "Tcell",
                                                   "cd8_tem" = "Tcell",
                                                   "Endothelial cells" = "Vasculature",
                                                   "HPD+ tumor" = "Tumor",
                                                   "Inflammatory CAFs" = "Fibroblast",
                                                   "Interferon-activated CAFs" = "Fibroblast",
                                                   "KRT16+ tumor" = "Tumor",
                                                   "ITGB6+ tumor" = "Tumor",
                                                   "Matrix fibroblasts" = "Fibroblast",
                                                   "Myofibroblasts" = "Fibroblast",
                                                   "Pericytes" = "Vasculature",
                                                   "PGC+ tumor" = "Tumor",
                                                   "Plasma_IgA" = "Plasma",
                                                   "Plasma_IgG" = "Plasma",
                                                   "Proliferating tumor" = "Tumor",
                                                   "Proliferating vasculature" = "Vasculature",
                                                   "TAM_M1like" = "Macrophage",
                                                   "TAM_M2like" = "Macrophage",
                                                   "TAM_SPP1" = "Macrophage")

# Save seurat object with cell types
results_list$seurat_file_postCellTyping <- paste0(objects_dir, "/seurat_object_postCellTyping.rds")
saveRDS(results_list, results_list_file)
saveRDS(seu.obj, results_list$seurat_file_postCellTyping)

```

```{r}
#| label: plot_major_minor_cellTypes
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| eval: false

for(ct in c("major_cell_type", "minor_cell_type")){

  # Plot it in XY space with random colors
  set.seed(2025)
  my_pal <- sample(colors(distinct = TRUE), length(unique(seu.obj@meta.data[,ct])))
  names(my_pal) <- unique(seu.obj@meta.data[,ct])
  ggplot(seu.obj@meta.data,
         aes(x = x_slide_mm, y = y_slide_mm, 
             color = get(ct))) +  
    geom_point(size = 0.001) +  
    scale_color_manual(values = my_pal, na.value = "lightgrey", name = ct) +
    theme_classic() +  
    coord_fixed() +  
    guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size=10)))
  ggsave(filename = paste0(celltyping_dir, "/Plots/XY_", ct, ".png"),
         width = 8, height = 16, units = "in")
  
  # Plot each cell type separately
  for (ct1 in unique(seu.obj@meta.data[,ct])){
    if(is.na(ct1)){next}
    ggplot(seu.obj@meta.data,
           aes(x = x_slide_mm, y = y_slide_mm)) +  
      geom_point(size = 0.05, color = "lightgrey") +  
      geom_point(data = seu.obj@meta.data %>% filter(get(ct) == ct1),
                 aes(x = x_slide_mm, y = y_slide_mm),
                 size = 0.05, color = "red") +
      theme_classic() +  
      coord_fixed() +  
      ggtitle(paste0(ct, ": ", ct1))
    ggsave(filename = paste0(celltyping_dir, "/Plots/XY_", ct, "_", ct1, ".png"),
           width = 8, height = 16, units = "in")
  }
  
  
  # Plot it in UMAP space
  DimPlot(seu.obj, group.by = ct, reduction = "umap", label = T) +
    scale_color_manual(values = my_pal, na.value = "lightgrey") + coord_fixed()
  ggsave(filename = paste0(celltyping_dir, "/Plots/umap_", ct, ".png"),
         width = 16, height = 12, units = "in")
  
  # Plot each cell type separately in UMAP space
  plot.df <- seu.obj@meta.data
  plot.df$UMAP1 <- seu.obj@reductions$umap@cell.embeddings[,1]
  plot.df$UMAP2 <- seu.obj@reductions$umap@cell.embeddings[,2]
  
  for (ct1 in unique(plot.df[,ct])){
    ggplot(plot.df,
           aes(x = UMAP1, y = UMAP2)) +  
      geom_point(size = 0.05, alpha = 0.5, color = "lightgrey") +  
      geom_point(data = plot.df %>% filter(get(ct) == ct1),
                 aes(x = UMAP1, y = UMAP2),
                 size = 0.05, color = "red") +
      theme_classic() +  
      coord_fixed() +  
      ggtitle(paste0(ct, ": ", ct1))
    ggsave(filename = paste0(celltyping_dir, "/Plots/UMAP_", ct, "_", ct1, ".png"),
           width = 10, height = 8, units = "in")
  }
  
  # Marker heatmap
  ## prepare data for marker gene heatmap:
  fc_subclus_ctl_gran <- clusterwise_foldchange_metrics(seu.obj[["RNA"]]@counts
                                                        ,metadata = seu.obj@meta.data
                                                        ,cluster_column = ct
  )
  # subtract background from the mean per-cluster expression profiles:
  neg_counts = seu.obj@assays$negprobes$counts
  for (name in unique(seu.obj@meta.data[,ct])) {
    if(is.na(name)){next}
    isthiscelltype <- seu.obj@meta.data[,ct] == name
    meannegthiscelltype <- Matrix::mean(neg_counts[, isthiscelltype])
    
    fc_subclus_ctl_gran$cluster_expr[fc_subclus_ctl_gran$cluster == name] <- 
      pmax(fc_subclus_ctl_gran$cluster_expr[fc_subclus_ctl_gran$cluster == name] - meannegthiscelltype, 0)
  }
  # create the heatmap:
  hm_lh <- add_ncells(marker_heatmap(fc_subclus_ctl_gran))
  
  png(filename = paste0(celltyping_dir, "/Plots/heatmap_", ct, "_negRemoved.png"),
      width = 24, height = 8, units = "in", res = 300)
  print(hm_lh)
  dev.off()
  
  # Save results file
  results_list[paste0(ct, "_color_pal")] <- my_pal
}
saveRDS(results_list, results_list_file)
```

### Save annotated data
Here we save annotated data into basic files for some of the downstream analyses that won't use the Seurat object.

```{r}
#| label: save_basic_files
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: true
#| eval: false

# if there's no seurat object, read it in
if (!("seu.obj" %in% ls())){
  seu.obj <- readRDS(results_list$seurat_file_postCellTyping)
}

# Save raw expression matrix
exp_mat <- seu.obj@assays$RNA$counts
saveRDS(exp_mat, file = paste0(objects_dir, "/raw_exp_mat.rds"))

# Save xy positions
xy <- seu.obj@meta.data[, c("x_slide_mm", "y_slide_mm")]
saveRDS(xy, file = paste0(objects_dir, "/xy.rds"))

# Save cell types
ct <- seu.obj@meta.data[, c("major_cell_type", "minor_cell_type")]
saveRDS(ct, file = paste0(objects_dir, "/cell_types.rds"))

```

## Publication Quality Plots

In this final section we include the code to make high quality plots that appear in the manuscript.

### Minor cell types
We make a nicer plot of the minor cell types, with cell type colors chosen to keep similar cell types in the same families.

```{r}
#| label: plot_minor_subtypes_xy
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| eval: false

if(!("seu.obj" %in% ls())){
  seu.obj <- readRDS(results_list$seurat_file_postCellTyping)
}

if("LUM+ tumor" %in% seu.obj$minor_cell_type){
  seu.obj$minor_cell_type <- dplyr::recode(
    seu.obj@meta.data$minor_cell_type,
    "LUM+ tumor" = "ITGB6+ tumor"
  )
}

# Set up hand-selected color palette
cell_colors <- c(
  # Tumor cells
  "HPD+ tumor" = "#E41A1C", "KRT16+ tumor" = "#FF6666", "ITGB6+ tumor" = "#FF9999",
  "PGC+ tumor" = "#CC3333", "Proliferating tumor" = "#FF4C4C",
  
  # CD4 T cells
  "cd4_naive" = "#377EB8", "cd4_tcm" = "#4DA3D4", "cd4_tem" = "#6BB7E3",
  "cd4_teff_th1" = "#2C7FB8", "cd4_teff_th2" = "#5AAAE6", "cd4_teff_th17" = "#8CCBF2",
  "cd4_treg" = "#1F78B4",
  
  # CD8 T cells
  "cd8_naive" = "#66C2A5", "cd8_tcm" = "#41AE76", "cd8_tem" = "#238B45",
  "cd8_teff_cytotoxic" = "#74C476", "cd8_exhausted" = "#A1D99B",
  
  # B cells & Plasma
  "bcell" = "#984EA3", "Plasma_IgA" = "#BEAED4", "Plasma_IgG" = "#CAB2D6",
  
  # Myeloid & innate
  "dendritic" = "#4DAF4A", "neutrophil" = "#78C679", "mast" = "#A6D96A",
  "nk" = "#66BD63", "innate_lymphoid" = "#31A354",
  
  # Macrophages
  "TAM_M1like" = "#FF7F00", "TAM_M2like" = "#FDB462", "TAM_SPP1" = "#E6550D",
  
  # Fibroblasts & CAFs
  "Inflammatory CAFs" = "#999999", "Interferon-activated CAFs" = "#BDBDBD",
  "Matrix fibroblasts" = "#D9D9D9", "Myofibroblasts" = "#737373",
  
  # Endothelial & vasculature
  "Endothelial cells" = "#9ECAE1", "Proliferating vasculature" = "#6BAED6",
  "Pericytes" = "#4292C6",
  
  # Necrotic & Unknown
  "Necrotic cells" = "#CCCCCC", "Unknown" = "#E0E0E0"
)
# Save these as manually formatted minor cell type colors
results_list$minor_cell_type_color_pal_manual <- cell_colors
saveRDS(results_list, results_list_file)

# Set cell type order to group similar types
seu.obj@meta.data$minor_cell_type <- factor(seu.obj@meta.data$minor_cell_type,
                                            levels = names(cell_colors))


# Plot in xy
ggplot(seu.obj@meta.data[idx,], aes(x_slide_mm, y_slide_mm, color = minor_cell_type)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.01) +
  scale_color_manual(values = cell_colors) +
  theme_void() +
  coord_fixed() +
  guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 5)))
ggsave(filename = paste0(celltyping_dir, "/Plots/XY_minorCellType_manualFormatting.png"),
       height = 8, width = 8, units = "in", dpi = 400)


# Plot two zoomed in regions with polygons
zooms = results_list$zoom_regions
meta <- seu.obj@meta.data
# Read in polygons
polygons <- fread(paste0(objects_dir, "/FlatFiles/flatFiles/BreastCancer/BreastCancer-polygons.csv.gz"))
polygons$x_slide_mm <- polygons$x_global_px * 0.12028/1000 # Pixel to mm conversion for commercial instrument
polygons$y_slide_mm <- polygons$y_global_px * 0.12028/1000

# Merge in ct
polygons <- merge(polygons, meta[,c("cell_ID", "minor_cell_type")], by.x = "cell", by.y = "cell_ID", all.y = T)

# Plot for each zoom region
for (zoom in zooms){
  
  
idx <- which(
  polygons$x_slide_mm > zoom$xmin &
  polygons$x_slide_mm < zoom$xmax &
  polygons$y_slide_mm > zoom$ymin &
  polygons$y_slide_mm < zoom$ymax
)

scale_bar <- make_scale_bar_r(polygons[idx, c("x_slide_mm")], polygons[idx, "y_slide_mm"])
  
  ggplot(polygons[idx,],
         aes(x_slide_mm, y_slide_mm, group = cell)) +
    geom_polygon(aes(fill = minor_cell_type)) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = cell_colors) +
    theme_void() +  
    coord_fixed() +  
    theme(legend.position = "none") +
    scale_bar$bg + 
    scale_bar$rect + 
    scale_bar$label
  ggsave(paste0(celltyping_dir, "/Plots/XY_minor_cell_types_zoomed_", zoom$region, ".png"),
         width = 4, height = 4, units = "in", dpi = 400)
}

# Heatmap with hand-selected color points and cell numbers
fc_subclus_ctl_gran <- clusterwise_foldchange_metrics(seu.obj[["RNA"]]@counts
                                                      ,metadata = seu.obj@meta.data
                                                      ,cluster_column = "minor_cell_type"
)
# subtract background from the mean per-cluster expression profiles:
neg_counts <- seu.obj@assays$negprobes$counts
for (name in unique(seu.obj@meta.data[,"minor_cell_type"])) {
  if(is.na(name)){next}
  isthiscelltype <- seu.obj@meta.data[,"minor_cell_type"] == name
  #isthiscelltype[is.na(isthiscelltype)] <- FALSE #NAs not handled well in subsetting in next step
  meannegthiscelltype <- Matrix::mean(neg_counts[, isthiscelltype])
  
  fc_subclus_ctl_gran$cluster_expr[fc_subclus_ctl_gran$cluster == name] <- 
    pmax(fc_subclus_ctl_gran$cluster_expr[fc_subclus_ctl_gran$cluster == name] - meannegthiscelltype, 0)
}
# create the heatmap:
hm_lh <- add_ncells(marker_heatmap(fc_subclus_ctl_gran))


# Extract the factor levels from the heatmap after add_ncells()
labels_with_counts <- levels(hm_lh$data$cluster)  # after add_ncells()

# Recover original names by stripping counts
original_names <- gsub(" \\(.*\\)$", "", labels_with_counts)

# Build dot data frame
dot_df <- data.frame(
  label = labels_with_counts,
  color = cell_colors[original_names],
  y = seq_along(labels_with_counts)  # matches factor order
)

# Add dots to the left of labels
hm_lh +
  geom_point(data = dot_df,
             aes(x = -0.5, y = y),  # adjust x for left margin
             color = dot_df$color, fill = dot_df$color,
             size = 2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "black") +
  #scale_y_continuous(breaks = dot_df$y, labels = dot_df$label) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +  # prevent clipping
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(hjust = 1, size = 8),
        plot.margin = margin(5, 5, 5, 5),  
        axis.line.y = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),legend.position = "top",
        legend.direction = "horizontal",
        legend.title.position = "top",
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
        legend.title = element_text(size = 8))
ggsave(filename = paste0(celltyping_dir, "/Plots/marker_heatmap_minor_cell_type_formatted.png"),
       width = 16, height = 8, units = "in", dpi = 400)


```

High quality spatial plot of minor cell types and two zoomed regions.

### Tumor subtypes

We make a nicer spatial plot of just the five tumor subtypes, using colors chosen to contrast well. There are very few ITGB6+ tumor cells, so in order to ensure that they're visible we plot them on top.
```{r}
#| label: plot_tumor_subtypes_xy
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| eval: false

if(!("seu.obj" %in% ls())){
  seu.obj <- readRDS(results_list$seurat_file_postCellTyping)
}

if("LUM+ tumor" %in% seu.obj$minor_cell_type){
  seu.obj$minor_cell_type <- dplyr::recode(
    seu.obj@meta.data$minor_cell_type,
    "LUM+ tumor" = "ITGB6+ tumor"
  )
}

# Use alphabet palette, but replace the dark fifth color with a brighter green
# Also replace the third brownish color with a brighter red
my_pal <- pals::alphabet(n = 5)
my_pal[5] <- alphabet(n=7)[7]
my_pal[3] <- alphabet(n=25)[15]
names(my_pal) <- grep("tumor", unique(seu.obj$minor_cell_type), value = T)


# Extract meta data
meta <- seu.obj@meta.data

# ITGB6+ tumor cells are very rare. Plot on top for visibility.

# Plot it
ggplot(meta %>% filter(major_cell_type != "Tumor"),
        aes(x = x_slide_mm, y = y_slide_mm)) +  
    geom_point(size = 0.01, color = "grey90") +  
  geom_point(data = meta %>% filter(major_cell_type == "Tumor"),
             aes(x_slide_mm, y_slide_mm, color = minor_cell_type),
             size = 0.01) +
   geom_point(data = meta %>% filter(minor_cell_type == "ITGB6+ tumor"),
             aes(x_slide_mm, y_slide_mm, color = minor_cell_type),
             size = 0.01) +
  scale_color_manual(values = my_pal, name = "Tumor subtype") +
    theme_void() +  
    coord_fixed() +  
    guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size=10))) +
  theme(legend.position = c(0,1),
        legend.justification = c(0, 1),
        legend.text=element_text(size=15),
        legend.title = element_text(size = 20))
ggsave(filename = paste0(celltyping_dir, "/Plots/XY_tumor_subclusters_highlighted.png"),
       width = 8, height = 14, units = "in")

# Plot two zoomed regions with polygons
if(is.null(results_list$zoom_regions)){
  zooms = list(
    
    "zoom1" = list('xmin' = 3.25,
                   'xmax' = 5.25,
                   'ymin' = 9,
                   'ymax' = 11,
                   'region' = 'i'),
    
    "zoom2" = list('xmin' = 2.5,
                   'xmax' = 4.5,
                   'ymin' = 3.5,
                   'ymax' = 5.5,
                   'region' = 'ii')
  )
  results_list$zoom_regions <- zooms
  saveRDS(results_list, results_list_file)
} else{
  zooms <- results_list$zoom_regions
}

# Read in polygons
polygons <- fread(paste0(objects_dir, "/FlatFiles/flatFiles/BreastCancer/BreastCancer-polygons.csv.gz"))
polygons$x_slide_mm <- polygons$x_global_px * 0.12028/1000
polygons$y_slide_mm <- polygons$y_global_px * 0.12028/1000

# Merge in ct
polygons <- merge(polygons, meta[,c("cell_ID", "minor_cell_type")], by.x = "cell", by.y = "cell_ID", all.y = T)

# Plot for each zoom region
for (zoom in zooms){
  
  idx <- which(
    polygons$x_slide_mm > zoom$xmin &
      polygons$x_slide_mm < zoom$xmax &
      polygons$y_slide_mm > zoom$ymin &
      polygons$y_slide_mm < zoom$ymax
  )
  
  scale_bar <- make_scale_bar_r(polygons[idx, c("x_slide_mm")], polygons[idx, "y_slide_mm"])
  
  ggplot(polygons[idx,],
         aes(x_slide_mm, y_slide_mm, group = cell)) +
    geom_polygon(data = polygons[idx,] %>% filter(!grepl("tumor", polygons[idx, "minor_cell_type"])),
                 aes(x_slide_mm, y_slide_mm, group = cell),
                 fill = "grey90") +
    geom_polygon(data = polygons[idx,] %>% filter(grepl("tumor", polygons[idx, "minor_cell_type"])),
                 aes(x_slide_mm, y_slide_mm, group = cell, fill = minor_cell_type)) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = my_pal) +
    theme_void() +  
    coord_fixed() +  
    theme(legend.position = "none") +
    scale_bar$bg + 
    scale_bar$rect + 
    scale_bar$label
  ggsave(paste0(celltyping_dir, "/Plots/XY_tumorsOnly_zoomed_", zoom$region, ".png"),
         width = 4, height = 4, units = "in", dpi = 400)
}

```

We also make a marker gene heatmap for the tumor subtypes. Use only genes expected to be more highly expressed in tumor cells, as identified with the smiDE overlap metric, than surrounding cells. 
```{r}
#| label: generate_tumor_heatmap
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| eval: false

if(!("seu.obj" %in% ls())){
  seu.obj <- readRDS(results_list$seurat_file_postCellTyping)
}

if("LUM+ tumor" %in% seu.obj$minor_cell_type){
  seu.obj$minor_cell_type <- dplyr::recode(
    seu.obj@meta.data$minor_cell_type,
    "LUM+ tumor" = "ITGB6+ tumor"
  )
}

# Identify genes to consider with overlap metric
overlap_metrics <- 
smiDE::overlap_ratio_metric(assay_matrix = seu.obj@assays$RNA$data,
                           metadata = meta,
                           cluster_col = "major_cell_type",
                           radius = 0.05,
                           #split_neighbors_by_colname = "Run_Tissue_name",
                           sdimx_col = "x_slide_mm",
                           sdimy_col = "y_slide_mm"
                           )
tumor_genes <- overlap_metrics[major_cell_type=="Tumor" & ratio <= 1]$target

## prepare data for marker gene heatmap:
idx = which(seu.obj$major_cell_type == "Tumor")
ct = "minor_cell_type"
fc_subclus_ctl_gran <- clusterwise_foldchange_metrics(seu.obj[["RNA"]]@counts[tumor_genes,idx]
                                                      ,metadata = seu.obj@meta.data[idx,]
                                                      ,cluster_column = ct
)
# subtract background from the mean per-cluster expression profiles:
negprobes = seu.obj@assays$negprobes$counts
for (name in unique(seu.obj@meta.data[idx,ct])) {
  if(is.na(name)){next}
  isthiscelltype <- seu.obj@meta.data[idx,ct] == name
  meannegthiscelltype <- Matrix::mean(negprobes[,idx][, isthiscelltype])
  
  fc_subclus_ctl_gran$cluster_expr[fc_subclus_ctl_gran$cluster == name] <- 
    pmax(fc_subclus_ctl_gran$cluster_expr[fc_subclus_ctl_gran$cluster == name] - meannegthiscelltype, 0)
}
# create the heatmap:
hm_lh <- marker_heatmap(fc_subclus_ctl_gran, topn = 6) +
  theme(
    legend.direction = "horizontal", # Arrange items within a legend horizontally
    legend.position = "bottom",    # Place the entire legend box at the bottom
    legend.box = "horizontal"      # Arrange multiple legend boxes horizontally
  )

png(filename = paste0(celltyping_dir, "/Plots/heatmap_", ct, "_tumorOnly_negRemoved.png"),
    width = 8, height = 3, units = "in", res = 300)
print(add_ncells(hm_lh))
dev.off()
```

```{r}
#| eval: true

knitr::include_graphics(paste0(celltyping_dir, "/Plots/heatmap_", "minor_cell_type", "_tumorOnly_negRemoved.png"))
```
